clusters.name: file_operations

tools.original_description: List directory contents with [FILE] or [DIR] prefixes
tools.enriched_description: Lists the contents of a specified directory, using [FILE] or [DIR] prefixes to categorize items. Use when needing to view directory structure. Key parameter: path.

tools.original_description: Read complete contents of a file
tools.enriched_description: Reads the complete contents of a specified file, useful for accessing file data in various applications. Key parameter: path.
Reads multiple files simultaneously from specified paths, useful for processing large datasets or gathering information from various sources efficiently.

tools.original_description:
Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path.
                        
                        Use this instead of 'execute_command' with ls/dir commands.
                        Results distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes.
                        Only works within allowed directories.
                        
                        IMPORTANT: Always use absolute paths (starting with '/' or drive letter like 'C:\') for reliability. Relative paths may fail as they depend on the current working directory. Tilde paths (~/...) might not work in all contexts. Unless the user explicitly asks for relative paths, use absolute paths.
                        This command can be referenced as "DC: ..." or "use Desktop Commander to ..." in your instructions.
tools.enriched_description: Lists all files and directories in a specified path, distinguishing between them. Use absolute paths for reliable results within allowed directories.

tools.original_description:
Read the contents of a file from the file system or a URL with optional offset and length parameters.
                        
                        Prefer this over 'execute_command' with cat/type for viewing files.
                        
                        Supports partial file reading with:
                        - 'offset' (start line, default: 0)
                        - 'length' (max lines to read, default: configurable via 'fileReadLineLimit' setting, initially 1000)
                        
                        When reading from the file system, only works within allowed directories.
                        Can fetch content from URLs when isUrl parameter is set to true
                        (URLs are always read in full regardless of offset/length).
                        
                        Handles text files normally and image files are returned as viewable images.
                        Recognized image types: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP.
                        
                        IMPORTANT: Always use absolute paths (starting with '/' or drive letter like 'C:\') for reliability. Relative paths may fail as they depend on the current working directory. Tilde paths (~/...) might not work in all contexts. Unless the user explicitly asks for relative paths, use absolute paths.
                        This command can be referenced as "DC: ..." or "use Desktop Commander to ..." in your instructions.
tools.enriched_description: Reads file contents from the file system or a URL, supporting optional offset and length for partial reading. Use when accessing text or image files.

clusters.name: git_vcs

tools.enriched_description: Retrieves and displays the commit logs for a specified repository, useful for tracking changes and understanding project history.
Displays the current status of the working tree, useful for tracking changes in files and understanding the state of the repository.

tools.original_description: Shows changes in the working directory that are not yet staged
tools.enriched_description: Displays unstaged changes in the working directory, useful for reviewing modifications before staging them for commit.

tools.original_description: Shows the contents of a commit
tools.enriched_description: Displays the contents of a specific commit, useful for reviewing changes and understanding project history.

tools.original_description: Gets commits of a branch in a repository
tools.enriched_description: Retrieves commits from a specified branch in a repository, useful for tracking changes and contributions. Key parameters include owner, repo, and sha.
Searches GitHub repositories based on a specified query, useful for finding relevant projects; supports pagination with parameters for page and perPage.

clusters.rationale: Tools have genuinely different functions (history vs status vs diff vs show) with similar short descriptions. Best cluster for proving that description enrichment helps reranker distinguish.

tools.original_description: Search for records containing specific text
tools.enriched_description: Searches for records in a specified table that contain a specific text, useful for retrieving relevant data based on defined criteria.

tools.original_description: Lists all tables in a specific base
tools.enriched_description: Lists all tables within a specified base, useful for retrieving table information based on the baseId and detailLevel parameters.

tools.original_description: Lists records from a specified Airtable table
tools.enriched_description: Lists records from a specified Airtable table based on given parameters, useful for retrieving specific data sets efficiently.

tools.original_description: Run a find query against a MongoDB collection
tools.enriched_description: Executes a find query on a MongoDB collection to retrieve documents based on specified criteria. Use it for data retrieval tasks.

tools.original_description: Describe the schema for a collection
tools.enriched_description: Describes the schema for a MongoDB collection, useful for understanding data structure and organization within the database.

tools.original_description: List all collections for a given database
tools.enriched_description: Lists all collections within a specified database, useful for retrieving database structure information and managing data organization.

clusters.rationale: Large cluster (300+ queries), enrichment degraded mongodb tools. Good test of whether targeted enrichment on one tool steers selection.
